findings.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
findings.summary:

findings.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
findings.summary: On November 18, 2026, nginx announced the availability of a fix for multiple critical vulnerabilities in nginx that could lead to remote code execution. These vulnerabilities affect nginx releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 and is fixed in releases 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable). These vulnerabilities were identified by the following CVEs: CVE-2026-113425: NGINX ngx_mail_proxy_module vulnerability CVE-2026-121810: NGINX ngx_http_v3_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123007: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123633: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123634: NGINX resolver vulnerability For more information, see the nginx Security Advisories . This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-nginx-nov-2026-e8jska2s Security Impact Rating: Critical CVE: CVE-2026-113425,CVE-2026-121810,CVE-2026-123007,CVE-2026-123633,CVE-2026-123634

findings.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
findings.summary:
A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG.

The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions.

The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,

findings.title: memtomem-stm: Concurrent LTM recovery can duplicate reconnects or reuse a cancelled transport session
findings.summary: Concurrent surfacing RPC failures can trigger more than one reconnect for the same dirty session, and cancellation during a post-reconnect retry can leave the replacement session reusable despite an interrupted protocol exchange. The private fix introduces monotonic session generations, one shielded shared reconnect flight per dirty generation, and generation-aware cancellation handling across search, access-count, and scratch RPCs. The duplicate-reconnect subcase was introduced in 0.1.24; cancellation recovery affects the broader listed range.

findings.title: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
findings.summary:
## Summary
A security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.

### Patches
* 2.5.1

### Impact
This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.

## Details
_Chain:_
1. `POST /tlm/query` writes the user-controlled `fields` value into `fields_in.txt` under the AIT-GUI static directory.
   *  If the supplied `dataDir` has no `.pcap` files, the route returns the expected `400 Bad Request` before deleting that file.
2. `POST /script/run` accepts `scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt`.
   * AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.

_Relevant code:_
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:930,935,942-944`: `/tlm/query` writes `fields` to `fields_in.txt`.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:952-958,978`: the no-PCAP error path aborts before cleanup.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1130-1136`: `/script/run` joins `scriptPath` with `ScriptRoot` and only checks that the path exists.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1186-1191`: the selected file is read and executed as Python.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1105-1108`: nearby `/scripts/load/<name>` has a path containment check, but `/script/run` does not.

### Fix Information
Restricted script execution paths and avoided using static temp files.

## PoC
1. `POST /tlm/query` writes the user-controlled `fields` value into `fields_in.txt` under the AIT-GUI static directory.
